scenarios.title: Clean settlement
scenarios.description: UTR present verbatim in the narration, amount exact, lands inside the T+2 window.

scenarios.title: UTR buried in narration
scenarios.description: The UTR is present but wrapped in bank-specific rail markers, counterparty names and a trailing balance.

scenarios.title: Narration clipped at field width
scenarios.description: The bank export truncates narration at 40 characters, cutting the UTR short. Only a prefix survives.

scenarios.title: Corrupted UTR
scenarios.description: Two adjacent characters of the UTR are transposed, as happens when a reference is re-keyed by hand into a payment portal.

scenarios.title: No reference at all
scenarios.description: The narration carries no recoverable reference. The amount and date are unique within the window, so it is still resolvable.

scenarios.title: Paise-level rounding drift
scenarios.description: The bank credit differs from the settlement by one or two paise, from the PSP and the bank rounding a fee split differently.

scenarios.title: Gross recovered from net
scenarios.description: Only the net credit is known. The gross is recovered by inverting the contracted rate card for the payment method.

scenarios.title: Several payouts, one credit
scenarios.description: The PSP nets three to six settlements into a single bank transfer. The component set has to be recovered by decomposition.

scenarios.title: One payout, several credits
scenarios.description: A large settlement arrives as two bank credits on the same or adjacent days, typically because it crossed an RTGS batch limit.

scenarios.title: Late but within slack
scenarios.description: The credit lands a day later than the contracted cycle, inside the tolerance the window allows.

scenarios.title: Settlement across a bank holiday
scenarios.description: T+2 spans Diwali, so the credit lands two calendar days later than a naive calendar window would predict.

scenarios.title: Capture just before IST midnight
scenarios.description: Captured at 23:45 UTC, which is the following day in IST. Bucketing on the UTC date puts it in the wrong batch entirely.

scenarios.title: Beyond the settlement SLA
scenarios.description: Identifier and amount agree, but the credit is far outside the contracted cycle. Matching it silently would hide an SLA breach.

scenarios.title: Refund netted off the payout
scenarios.description: A refund issued during the cycle is deducted from the payout, so the credit is smaller than the sum of its payments. The payout must still reconcile once the refund is taken into account.

scenarios.title: Chargeback deducted
scenarios.description: A disputed payment is clawed back mid-cycle, reducing the payout by the disputed amount plus a dispute fee. Both deductions must be accounted for.

scenarios.title: Chargeback for an out-of-period payment
scenarios.description: A deduction appears for a payment captured before the period under review, so nothing in scope explains it.

scenarios.title: Refund for an out-of-period payment
scenarios.description: A refund nets off a payout but its original payment predates the batch.

scenarios.title: Payout never arrived
scenarios.description: The PSP reports a settlement that has no corresponding bank credit. Either the feed lags or the money is on hold.

scenarios.title: Credit from outside the PSP
scenarios.description: A direct customer NEFT or an inter-account sweep that no settlement explains. Not an error, but it must not be force-matched.

scenarios.title: Undisclosed deduction
scenarios.description: Identifier and date agree but the credit is materially short, with no documented refund or adjustment to account for it.

scenarios.title: Two identical payouts, no reference
scenarios.description: Two settlements of exactly the same amount on the same day, neither carrying a recoverable UTR. No evidence distinguishes them.

scenarios.title: Paise/rupee unit slip
scenarios.description: One side reports the amount 100x off -- a currency-unit bug between the PSP API and the accounting export.

scenarios.title: Transposed digits
scenarios.description: The amount has two digits swapped relative to its counterpart, the signature of manual entry.

scenarios.title: Same UTR on two credits
scenarios.description: One UTR appears on two bank lines. One of them is a double-post, and matching both would overstate cash.

scenarios.title: Fee above the rate card
scenarios.description: The PSP charged more commission than the negotiated rate allows. Recoverable money that a match-only reconciler never notices.

scenarios.title: International settlement
scenarios.description: A USD payment settled in INR at a rate that cannot be independently verified from the data supplied.

scenarios.title: Collected but not booked
scenarios.description: Money was collected and settled, but the internal ledger has no entry. Revenue is currently unrecorded.

scenarios.title: Partial settlement
scenarios.description: Part of the payment settled and the balance is retained as a reserve, to be released in a later cycle.

scenarios.title: Unparseable field
scenarios.description: A corrupted amount field in the export. The record must be quarantined and excluded from totals, never coerced to zero.

scenarios.title: Credit reversed the same day
scenarios.description: A credit and an identical debit that cancel out -- a failed transfer that was returned. Both lines must net to nothing, not become two breaks.
